# Setup 
Prior the running anything below, you must set your working directory to this folder's directory. 

```{r}
# Load package
# Make sure you install.packages in a separate R script to install the relevant packages
library(tidyverse)
```

!! READ THIS: Make sure you clear / reset your global environment variables before running each block of code since each block is designed to work independently of each other. 

# State Event Proportions
Used by the Donut chart to graph the proportions of event categories in each state, also used by the lollipop chart to get the total number of events in state. 
```{r}
## For Choropleth Map - State-level Proportion of Events over Total Events in Australia
# Read the original event-level CSV
events <- read.csv(
  "Australian_Cultural_Events_List_2026.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Aggregate events by State
state_proportions <- events %>%
  group_by(State) %>%
  summarise(
    Event_Count = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Proportion = Event_Count / sum(Event_Count)
  )

# Output the aggregated CSV
write.csv(
  state_proportions,
  "state_event_proportions.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Display the result
print(state_proportions)
```

# State Category Count 
Aggregates the number of instances of events under category Arts & Culture, Sports and Indigenous for every State and Territory in Australia. Used for the radar chart. 

```{r}
# 1. Read the original events dataset
input_file <- "Australian_Cultural_Events_List_2026.csv"

events <- read_csv(
  input_file,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# 2. Define the eight Australian states and territories
state_order <- c(
  "Australian Capital Territory",
  "New South Wales",
  "Northern Territory",
  "Queensland",
  "South Australia",
  "Tasmania",
  "Victoria",
  "Western Australia"
)

# Support both full state names and common abbreviations
state_lookup <- c(
  "ACT" = "Australian Capital Territory",
  "NSW" = "New South Wales",
  "NT"  = "Northern Territory",
  "QLD" = "Queensland",
  "SA"  = "South Australia",
  "TAS" = "Tasmania",
  "VIC" = "Victoria",
  "WA"  = "Western Australia"
)

# 3. Select the three categories used in the radar chart
categories <- c(
  "Arts & Culture",
  "Sports",
  "Indigenous"
)

# 4. Standardise state names and filter the required categories
events_filtered <- events %>%
  mutate(
    State = trimws(as.character(State)),
    State = if_else(
      State %in% names(state_lookup),
      unname(state_lookup[State]),
      State
    ),
    Category = trimws(as.character(Category))
  ) %>%
  filter(
    State %in% state_order,
    Category %in% categories
  )

# 5. Count events for each state and category
state_category_counts <- events_filtered %>%
  count(State, Category, name = "Event_Count")

# 6. Create all 24 combinations and fill missing counts with zero
radar_data <- expand_grid(
  State = state_order,
  Category = categories
) %>%
  left_join(
    state_category_counts,
    by = c("State", "Category")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Event_Count = replace_na(Event_Count, 0L),
    State = factor(State, levels = state_order),
    Category = factor(Category, levels = categories)
  ) %>%
  arrange(State, Category) %>%
  mutate(
    State = as.character(State),
    Category = as.character(Category)
  )

# 7. Export the aggregated CSV
output_file <- "radar_state_category_counts.csv"

write_csv(radar_data, output_file)

# 8. Display the result for verification
print(radar_data, n = 24)

cat("\nCSV successfully generated at:", output_file, "\n")
cat("Number of rows:", nrow(radar_data), "\n")

# Check that all combinations are present
stopifnot(
  nrow(radar_data) == 24,
  !anyDuplicated(radar_data[c("State", "Category")]),
  all(radar_data$Event_Count >= 0)
)
```

# Daily Event Density in 2026
Aggregates the sum of all events occurring on all dates from the year 2026, calculating as the event density. This counts events taking place on that day, not just the starting dates, which will overlay events spanning multiple days or months. 

```{r}
# 1. Read the original event dataset
events <- read_csv(
  "Australian_Cultural_Events_List_2026.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# 2. Convert event dates and prepare the date ranges
events <- events %>%
  mutate(
    Start_Date = as.Date(Start_Date),
    End_Date = as.Date(End_Date)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(Start_Date),
    !is.na(End_Date),
    Start_Date <= as.Date("2026-12-31"),
    End_Date >= as.Date("2026-01-01"),
    Start_Date <= End_Date
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Clip dates to 2026 for counting only
    Count_Start = pmax(Start_Date, as.Date("2026-01-01")),
    Count_End   = pmin(End_Date, as.Date("2026-12-31"))
  )

# 3. Expand each event into its active dates in 2026
event_dates <- events %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    Date = list(seq.Date(
      from = Count_Start,
      to = Count_End,
      by = "day"
    ))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(Date) %>%
  unnest(Date)

# 4. Count the number of active events for each day
daily_counts <- event_dates %>%
  count(Date, name = "Event_Count")

# 5. Generate a complete calendar for 2026,
#    including days with zero active events
calendar <- tibble(
  Date = seq.Date(
    from = as.Date("2026-01-01"),
    to = as.Date("2026-12-31"),
    by = "day"
  )
) %>%
  left_join(daily_counts, by = "Date") %>%
  mutate(
    Event_Count = replace_na(Event_Count, 0L),
    Month = month(Date, label = TRUE, abbr = FALSE),
    Month_Number = month(Date),
    Day = day(Date),

    # Monday = 0, Tuesday = 1, ..., Sunday = 6
    Weekday = wday(Date, week_start = 1) - 1,
    Weekday_Label = factor(
      c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")[Weekday + 1],
      levels = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")
    ),

    # Week column within each month, starting at 0.
    # Monday is the first day of each calendar week.
    Week_Of_Month = (
      Day + wday(floor_date(Date, "month"), week_start = 1) - 2
    ) %/% 7
  ) %>%
  select(
    Date,
    Event_Count,
    Month,
    Month_Number,
    Day,
    Weekday,
    Weekday_Label,
    Week_Of_Month
  )

# 6. Export the aggregated dataset to the same directory
write_csv(calendar, "event_density_daily_2026.csv")

# 7. Optional: inspect the output
print(calendar, n = 10)
cat("\nRows exported:", nrow(calendar), "\n")
cat("Total days:", n_distinct(calendar$Date), "\n")
```

# Calculate the average event duration 
```{r}
events <- read_csv(
  "Australian_Cultural_Events_List_2026.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

median(events$Duration_Days)
mean(events$Duration_Days)
```
